title: Hyundai and Kia Recall 14 EVs Over SK On Battery Cell Fire Risk
detail: Hyundai and Kia issued twin recalls covering just 14 vehicles combined — six 2023–2024 Ioniq 5 units and seven 2022–2024 EV6 plus one 2024 EV9 — over defective SK On battery cells with misaligned electrodes that could cause an internal short circuit and fire. Until repairs are completed, owners are told to limit charging to 80% state of charge and park outdoors, away from structures. Hyundai VINs became searchable on NHTSA.gov July 3, 2026; Kia VINs follow July 17, 2026. Owner notification letters are expected August 7 (Kia) and August 31 (Hyundai). The tiny recall population underscores how narrowly the defect was traced to a specific manufacturing batch.
